hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Yahya: I heard Malik saying: According to our understanding, regarding a slave who finds lost property and consumes it before the prescribed period elapses (which is one year): the lost property is the responsibility of his neck - either his master gives him the price of what his slave consumed, or he delivers his slave to them. But if he keeps it until the prescribed period for lost property elapses and then consumes it, it becomes a debt upon him that can be pursued, and it is not the responsibility of his neck, and there is nothing upon his master regarding it.

hadiths.arabicText: @ قَالَ /22 يَحْيَى /22 : سَمِعْتُ /12 مَالِكًا /12 ، يَقُولُ : /10 الْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا فِي الْعَبْدِ يَجِدُ اللُّقَطَةَ فَيَسْتَهْلِكُهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَبْلُغَ الْأَجَلَ الَّذِي أُجِّلَ فِي اللُّقَطَةِ ، وَذَلِكَ سَنَةٌ ، أَنَّهَا فِي رَقَبَتِهِ ، إِمَّا أَنْ يُعْطِيَ سَيِّدُهُ ثَمَنَ مَا اسْتَهْلَكَ غُلَامُهُ ، وَإِمَّا أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ إِلَيْهِمْ غُلَامَهُ ، وَإِنْ أَمْسَكَهَا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ الْأَجَلُ الَّذِي أُجِّلَ فِي اللُّقَطَةِ ، ثُمَّ اسْتَهْلَكَهَا ، كَانَتْ دَيْنًا عَلَيْهِ يُتْبَعُ بِهِ ، وَلَمْ تَكُنْ فِي رَقَبَتِهِ ، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى سَيِّدِهِ فِيهَا شَيْءٌ

Thabit said to him: It has occupied me from my livelihood. Umar said to him: 'Release it where you found it.'

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ /94 ابْنَ شِهَابٍ /94 ، يَقُولُ : /27 " كَانَتْ ضَوَالُّ الْإِبِلِ فِي زَمَانِ /93 عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ /93 إِبِلًا مُؤَبَّلَةً تَنَاتَجُ لَا يَمَسُّهَا أَحَدٌ ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ زَمَانُ /93 عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ /93 /20 " أَمَرَ بِتَعْرِيفِهَا ثُمَّ تُبَاعُ ، فَإِذَا جَاءَ صَاحِبُهَا أُعْطِيَ ثَمَنَهَا "

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Malik: from Said ibn Amr ibn Shurahhil ibn Said ibn Ubada, from his father, from his grandfather (Sa'd ibn Ubada), that Sa'd ibn Ubada went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in one of his expeditions, and his mother was seized by death in Medina. They said to her: Make a will. She said: In what should I make a will? The wealth is only Sa'd's wealth. She died before Sa'd returned. When Sa'd ibn Ubada returned, it was mentioned to him, and Sa'd said: O Messenger of Allah! Will it benefit her if I give charity on her behalf? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Yes. Sa'd said: The garden/property such and such is charity on her behalf.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 سَعِيدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُرَحْبِيلَ بْنِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ سَعْدِ بْنِ عُبَادَةَ /94 ، عَنْ /26 أَبِيهِ /26 ، عَنْ /26 جَدِّهِ /26 ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : /27 خَرَجَ سَعْدُ بْنُ عُبَادَةَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي بَعْضِ مَغَازِيهِ ، فَحَضَرَتْ أُمَّهُ الْوَفَاةُ /60 بِالْمَدِينَةِ /60 ، فَقِيلَ لَهَا : أَوْصِي . فَقَالَتْ : فِيمَ أُوصِي ؟ إِنَّمَا الْمَالُ مَالُ سَعْدٍ . فَتُوُفِّيَتْ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقْدَمَ سَعْدٌ ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ سَعْدُ بْنُ عُبَادَةَ ذُكِرَ ذَلِكَ لَهُ ، فَقَالَ سَعْدٌ : يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ، /20 " هَلْ يَنْفَعُهَا أَنْ أَتَصَدَّقَ عَنْهَا ؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : نَعَمْ "

May I give charity on her behalf?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Yes.'

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، /27 أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ الْأَنْصَارِ مِنْ بَنِي الْحَارِثِ بْنِ الْخَزْرَجِ تَصَدَّقَ عَلَى أَبَوَيْهِ بِصَدَقَةٍ ، فَهَلَكَا فَوَرِثَ ابْنُهُمَا الْمَالَ وَهُوَ نَخْلٌ ، فَسَأَلَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَقَالَ : /20 " قَدْ أُجِرْتَ فِي صَدَقَتِكَ ، وَخُذْهَا بِمِيرَاثِكَ "

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Malik: from Nafi, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'There is no right for any Muslim man who has something in which to make a will to sleep for two nights without his will being written and kept with him.' Malik said: The agreed upon matter among us is that if a testator makes a will in his health or illness with a will in which there is freeing of slaves from his slaves or other things, he can change from that what occurs to him, and he can do with it what he wishes until he dies, and if he desires to discard that will and replace it, he does so, except that if he designates a slave for freedom after his death, if he does so, there is no way to change what he designated. That is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'There is no right for any Muslim man who has something in which to make a will to sleep for two nights without his will being written and kept with him.' Malik said: If the testator had no ability to change his will, and what is mentioned in it of freeing slaves, then every testator would have bound his wealth that he willed from the freeing of slaves and other things, and a man may make a will in his health and at the time of his travel. Malik said: The matter among us which has no disagreement is that he can change from it what he wishes except for the designation of the slave for freedom.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 نَافِعٍ /94 ، /27 عَنْ /93 عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ /93 ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : /20 " مَا حَقُّ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ لَهُ شَيْءٌ يُوصَى فِيهِ يَبِيتُ لَيْلَتَيْنِ ، إِلَّا وَوَصِيَّتُهُ عِنْدَهُ مَكْتُوبَةٌ "

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Malik: from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm, from his father, that Amr ibn Sulaym al-Zurqi informed him, that a young man from Ghassanides, who had not reached puberty, from Ghassanid territory, and his heir was in Syria, and he was a man of wealth, had only a paternal cousin there. They said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: Here is a boy not yet pubescent from Ghassanides, and his heir is in Syria, and he has wealth, and there is no one for him here except his paternal cousin. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'Let him make a will for her.' He made a will for her with a property called Bir Jusham. Amr ibn Sulaym said: That property was sold for thirty thousand dirhams, and the paternal cousin for whom he made the will is the mother of Amr ibn Sulaym al-Zurqi.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ حَزْمٍ /94 ، عَنْ /26 أَبِيهِ /26 ، أَنَّ /26 عَمْرَو بْنَ سُلَيْمٍ الزُّرَقِيَّ /26 أَخْبَرَهُ ، أَنَّهُ /27 قِيلَ لِعُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ : إِنَّ هَاهُنَا غُلَامًا يَفَاعًا لَمْ يَحْتَلِمْ مِنْ غَسَّانَ وَوَارِثُهُ /60 بِالشَّامِ /60 ، وَهُوَ ذُو مَالٍ ، وَلَيْسَ لَهُ هَاهُنَا إِلَّا ابْنَةُ عَمٍّ لَهُ . قَالَ /93 عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ /93 : /20 " فَلْيُوصِ لَهَا " .

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Malik: from Yahya ibn Said, from Abi Bakr ibn Hazm, that a young man from Ghassanid territory, death was approaching him in Medina, and his heir was in Syria. This was mentioned to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and it was said to him: Such and such a man is dying, should he make a will? He said: 'Let him make a will.' Yahya ibn Said said: Abi Bakr said: And the boy was ten years old or twelve years old. He said: So he made a will with Bir Jusham, and his people sold it for thirty thousand dirhams. Yahya said: I heard Malik saying: The agreed upon matter among us is that the weak in intellect and the foolish and the stricken one who regains consciousness sometimes have valid wills if they retain from their intellect what they know about what they are willing, but as for one who does not retain from his intellect what recognizes what he is willing and is overcome in his intellect, he has no will.

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ /94 ، عَنْ /26 أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ حَزْمٍ /26 ، /27 أَنَّ " غُلَامًا مِنْ غَسَّانَ حَضَرَتْهُ الْوَفَاةُ /60 بِالْمَدِينَةِ /60 ، وَوَارِثُهُ /60 بِالشَّامِ /60 ، فَذُكِرَ ذَلِكَ لِعُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ : إِنَّ فُلَانًا يَمُوتُ ، أَفَيُوصِي ؟ قَالَ : /20 " فَلْيُوصِ "

critical_findings: Most hadiths are from Malik's Muwatta with strong, direct chains
One mursal report (hadith 9505) weakens it to 'Weak But Might Be Acceptable' category
One chain involves Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri who is classified as mudallis by some scholars, but remains highly reliable overall
Most chains feature Thiqah Thabt (highly reliable) narrators with explicit transmission terms
Primary topics cover legal rulings on lost property, charity for the deceased, and will/testament regulations
All hadiths relate to judicial issues and companion practices during early Islamic period
